claims.statement: Swapping equal red/blue material inside one averaging cell can leave the regional summary unchanged while reversing left/right; the ordered full pixel representation retains this difference.
claims.location: course/chapters/11.md:488,503; practical_order.svg title/desc and same-summary panel
claims.scope: Specific equal-size synthetic bars in the same grid cell. Regional average preserves coarser between-cell position; flatten is an ordered value array, not a trained spatial understanding mechanism.

evidence.supports: Each output channel is the within-bin sum divided by bin height and width; permutations inside the bin leave these means unchanged.
32→4 gives width8 bins so the swap remains inside one bin.
Flatten preserves element order; it does not compute an order-invariant average.

evidence.locator: §3.1 pp.3–4, Eq.(1), position embedding and Inductive bias paragraphs
evidence.supports: Position representations allow spatial information to be retained and learned; preserving material does not establish successful learned spatial relation use.
Exact mean invariance and distinguishability argument; no function of two identical pooled inputs can distinguish this swapped pair.

claims.statement: A list of object names does not determine who holds a cup or its spatial relation. Relation questions need appropriate images/questions/answers; boxes can provide position, and image feature sequences can support learned relations.
claims.scope: Representation and training options, not guaranteed accuracy. Boxes locate objects but do not alone establish every action; a learned visual sequence needs positional information and task supervision. The later limited apparel example is a proposed task design, not an accepted trained capability.

evidence.supports: Visual QA targets particular image information and specific spatial relations beyond generic captions/object names.

evidence.locator: §3 pp.3–4: box object concepts/spatial locations and conversation object actions/relative positions
evidence.supports: Primary example of position evidence and image-grounded relation question/answer material.
Projects whole-image grid features to a sequence of visual tokens and trains answer prediction from image plus question.

evidence.locator: §3.1 pp.3–4 Eq.(1), position embeddings and Inductive bias
evidence.supports: Position embeddings retain spatial information; spatial relations are learned, not automatically established by preserving image sequence.

The same object-name set is compatible with different relative positions/actions. The 11.17 current context explicitly retains object and grid position and labels hoped-for answers as design examples.

limitations.details: This is a deterministic synthetic information-flow counterexample. No model load, backward/update, full training, existing-model re-evaluation, model/data download, GPU, paid work or neural.pt save. Same-cell permutation is the condition; between-cell moves remain visible. Boxes/grid sequences are design options requiring appropriate evidence and learning; later limited apparel content is a plan, not an acceptance result. Fresh technical review is not blind reader testing; no claim about actual student comprehension.
